clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 11094 state the order's subject, assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Farm Credit Administration, the Export-Import Bank of Washington, the Board of Directors of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Administrator of the Small Business Administration and the Administrator of Veterans Affairs, and the authority under which the President acted, including Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958; they operate only through the numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 11094 directs the eight named heads of agencies, referred to collectively as Heads of agencies, to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs covering the functions assigned to them in the order, designed to develop a state of readiness for all conditions of national emergency. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 2 of EO 11094 directs the Federal Reserve Board, the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Farm Credit Administration and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation board to participate with the Office of Emergency Planning, the Department of the Treasury and other agencies in formulating emergency financial and stabilization policies, and sets out lettered paragraphs on money and credit, financial institutions, liquidity, cash withdrawals and credit transfers, and insurance. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 3 of EO 11094 directs the Heads of agencies, as appropriate, to participate with the Office of Emergency Planning and the Department of the Treasury in developing policies, plans and procedures for sharing war losses. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 4 of EO 11094 directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to collaborate with the Secretary of the Treasury in developing emergency financial control plans, programs, procedures and regulations on stock trading, modified trading, protection of securities, and the flow and flight of capital. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 5 of EO 11094 directs the Export-Import Bank of Washington to develop plans for using the Bank's resources under foreign policy guidance of the Secretary of State and under guidance of the Secretary of the Treasury. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 6 of EO 11094 directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to carry out functions set out in lettered paragraphs on prime contract authority, resource information, procurement, loans for plant modernization, resource pools and financial assistance. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 7 of EO 11094 directs the Administrator of Veterans Affairs to carry out health functions, assisting the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, and veterans benefits functions. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 8 of EO 11094 directs the Heads of agencies, within the framework of Federal research objectives, to supervise, conduct or recommend research directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness responsibilities, to designate representatives for necessary ad hoc or task force groups, and to provide advice and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in areas involving their agency's interest. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 9 of EO 11094 directs the Heads of agencies, as appropriate and in consonance with the national civil defense plans, programs and operations of the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, to provide facilities protection guidance material and to carry out damage assessment. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 10 of EO 11094 sets the guidance by which the Heads of agencies, in carrying out the functions assigned in the order, are to be guided: interagency cooperation (enlisting State authorities and coordinating with departments and agencies having related functions), Presidential coordination (the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning is to advise and assist the President), and emergency planning. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 11 of EO 11094 provides that nothing in the order is to be construed as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or developed pursuant to the order, and states that such authority is reserved to the President. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 12 of EO 11094 directs the Heads of agencies to provide for appropriate participation in the national resources evaluation program administered by the Office of Emergency Planning. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 13 of EO 11094 authorizes the Heads of agencies to redelegate within their agencies the functions assigned to them in the order. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The first sentence of Section 14 of EO 11094 provides that, to the extent of any inconsistency between the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this order, the latter controls. That rule was a continuing command and stayed in force while the order did. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11094: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (21), "Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The remaining sentence of Section 14 of EO 11094 revokes Emergency Preparedness Order No. 10 (issued by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization) and Defense Mobilization Orders No. 1-20, No. 1-22 and No. 1-24 (issued by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization). It is a one-time act that was complete when the order was issued; nothing in it continued afterwards. The held text of EO 11094, signed John F. Kennedy on February 26, 1963 at the White House, carries the revocation, so it was performed on that date (no later event is needed). The order as a whole was later revoked on 1969-10-28, but this one-time act had been completed on 1963-02-26.

research_rationale:
EO 11094 (1963-02-26; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and seven other agencies) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (28 FR 1855, Federal Register of 1963-02-28), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the John F. Kennedy signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 16 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Section 14 is split in two: its first sentence (precedence over inconsistent prior orders) and its closing sentence, which revokes Emergency Preparedness Order No. 10 (issued by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization) and Defense Mobilization Orders No. 1-20, No. 1-22 and No. 1-24 (issued by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization). Its own terms contain no end date, expiry or termination condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (21), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. No amendment, suspension or other instrument naming it is held besides EO 11490, which revokes it. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (21) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 11094. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
